classification.difficultyReason: Construct overlapping regions from inclusive totals, then calculate exclusive-region and neither probabilities.

content.prompt:
Use an appropriate Venn diagram.

In a group of 100 students, 60 study mathematics, 70 study physics and 30 study both mathematics and physics.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Represent this information on a Venn diagram.

answer.short: $M$: mathematics; $P$: physics. Mathematics only: $30$; both: $30$; physics only: $40$; neither: $0$.
answer.worked:
Let $M$ denote mathematics and $P$ denote physics. Place $30$ in the intersection.

$$\begin{align*}n(M\cap P^c)&=60-30\\n(M\cap P^c)&=30\\n(P\cap M^c)&=70-30\\n(P\cap M^c)&=40\\n((M\cup P)^c)&=100-(30+30+40)\\n((M\cup P)^c)&=0\end{align*}$$

spec.mathematics: Mathematics only 30, intersection 30, physics only 40, neither 0; total 100.

children.label: b
children.prompt: One student is selected at random from the group. What is the probability that the student studies:

answer.worked:
The mathematics-only region contains $60-30=30$ students.

$$\begin{align*}P(M\cap P^c)&=\frac{30}{100}\\P(M\cap P^c)&=\frac{3}{10}\end{align*}$$

The physics-only region contains $70-30=40$ students.

$$\begin{align*}P(P\cap M^c)&=\frac{40}{100}\\P(P\cap M^c)&=\frac{2}{5}\end{align*}$$

The three regions inside the circles contain $30+30+40=100$ students, so no students study neither subject.

$$\begin{align*}P((M\cup P)^c)&=\frac{100-100}{100}\\P((M\cup P)^c)&=0\end{align*}$$
